cars.generation: Original AM116 Indy production-road V8 GT family
cars.variant: 4200 five-speed manual — original 1969 factory heritage reference
cars.specification_market: Original 4,136 cc AM116 road specification, with the standard five-speed manual identified by the factory’s 2019 retrospective. The 4.7/4.9 engines, optional automatic, later Citroen hydraulic brakes and years do not add counts. Conflicting later power/speed/production figures, power-peak rpm, weight and unverified performance are omitted. The name honours 8CTF Indianapolis victories; the Indy road coupe did not win those races.
cars.summary: The Indy extended Maserati’s sporting V8 GT tradition into a genuine four-seat Vignale coupe, combining twin-cam engine engineering with long-distance usability. A first-hand drive records the original 4.2-litre engine’s strong upper-rev response and fast touring character. It belongs as a distinct historic Maserati performance GT, not simply through its badge or the Indianapolis-inspired name.

cars.generation: Original Tasmin / wedge-shaped production-road sports-car family
cars.variant: 350i V8 open car — original 1983 programme, club technical reference
cars.specification_market: 350i V8 road reference using the TVR Car Club technical table, within the original Tasmin/wedge programme. Club 190 bhp is retained without an invented SAE/DIN/net standard; a retrospective guide’s 197-bhp caption is not silently substituted. V6 Tasmin gearbox and suspension details, modified ECU settings, later wedge hardware and performance estimates are excluded. One family includes 280i/350i and related wedge variants, not extra counts for engine changes or the dropped Tasmin name.
cars.summary: The Tasmin wedge marked a major design and chassis departure for TVR. Installing the Rover V8 created the 350i and established the marque’s defining V8 sports-car direction under Peter Wheeler. Its light sports-car concept and lasting place in TVR history justify one wedge-family entry, grouping its engines, body revisions and renamed variants rather than treating them as extra cars.

facts.title: Why this car belongs
facts.explanation: The Tasmin wedge marked a major design and chassis departure for TVR. Installing the Rover V8 created the 350i and established the marque’s defining V8 sports-car direction under Peter Wheeler. Its light sports-car concept and lasting place in TVR history justify one wedge-family entry, grouping its engines, body revisions and renamed variants rather than treating them as extra cars.
